ruleSummary: The speed limit is 25 mph within 500 feet of a school while children are outside or crossing the street.
details: Some school zones may have speed limits as low as 15 mph, which will be indicated by signage.
exceptions: If the school grounds have no fence and children are outside, never drive faster than 25 mph.

ruleSummary: The speed limit for a blind intersection is 15 mph.
details: An intersection is considered 'blind' if there are no stop signs at any corner and you cannot see for 100 feet in either direction during the last 100 feet before crossing.

ruleSummary: The speed limit in any alley is 15 mph.
The speed limit is 15 mph within 100 feet of a railroad crossing where you cannot see the tracks for 400 feet in both directions.
details: You may drive faster than 15 mph if the crossing is controlled by gates, a warning signal, or a flag man.
exceptions: Controlled crossings allow speeds higher than 15 mph depending on the posted limit.

ruleSummary: Pedestrians have the right-of-way in marked or unmarked crosswalks.
details: If a pedestrian makes eye contact, they are ready to cross the street. Yield to them.
exceptions: Pedestrians must not suddenly leave a curb and walk or run into the path of a vehicle that is so close as to constitute an immediate hazard.
section: Laws and Rules of the Road

ruleSummary: It is illegal to park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant or a fire station driveway.
A red curb means no stopping, standing, or parking.
details: Buses may stop at a red zone marked for buses.
exceptions: Transit buses are exempt at designated bus stops.

ruleSummary: It is illegal for a person 21 years of age or older to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher.
details: You can still be convicted of a DUI if your BAC is below 0.08% but your driving is impaired.

ruleSummary: It is illegal for a person under 21 years of age to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.01% or higher.
details: California has a strict Zero Tolerance law for underage drivers.

ruleSummary: It is illegal for a person to drive a commercial vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.04% or higher.
You must stop from either direction until children are safely across the street and the red lights on the school bus stop flashing.
details: Failing to stop can result in a fine up to $1,000 and suspended driving privilege for 1 year.
exceptions: You do not need to stop if the school bus is on the other side of a divided or multilane highway (two or more lanes in each direction).
section: Laws and Rules of the Road

ruleSummary: You should signal at least 100 feet before you turn.
details: On a freeway, you should signal for at least 5 seconds before changing lanes.

ruleSummary: You must use your headlights 30 minutes after sunset and leave them on until 30 minutes before sunrise.
details: You must also turn them on anytime you cannot clearly recognize a person or vehicle from 1000 feet away.

ruleSummary: You must turn on your low-beam headlights if weather conditions require you to use your windshield wipers.
details: This applies to rain, snow, fog, or dust.

ruleSummary: It is against the law for a minor to use a cell phone or electronic wireless communications device while driving.
exceptions: Exceptions exist for calling emergency services (911) in an emergency situation.

ruleSummary: Use the '3-second rule' to avoid tailgating.
details: When the vehicle ahead of you passes a certain point, such as a sign, count 'one-thousand-one, one-thousand-two, one-thousand-three.' If you pass the same point before you finish counting, you are following too closely.
exceptions: Allow a 4-second or more following distance when tailgated, driving on slippery roads, or following motorcyclists/bicyclists on wet or icy roads.

ruleSummary: Use the hand-to-hand steering method (push/pull) for most turning maneuvers.
details: Your hands should be placed at 9 and 3 o'clock, or slightly lower at 8 and 4 o'clock.
exceptions: Hand-over-hand steering is recommended when turning at low speeds, parking, or recovering from a skid.

ruleSummary: At a T-intersection without STOP or YIELD signs, vehicles on the through road have the right-of-way.
details: Traffic on the terminating road must yield to traffic on the continuing crossroad.
section: Laws and Rules of the Road

ruleSummary: When two vehicles meet on a steep narrow road where neither can pass, the vehicle facing downhill must yield the right-of-way by backing up.
details: The vehicle facing downhill has the greater amount of control when backing up.
section: Laws and Rules of the Road

ruleSummary: You may make a U-turn in a residential district if there are no vehicles approaching you within 200 feet.
details: You may also make a U-turn whenever a traffic sign, light, or traffic signal protects you from approaching vehicles.
exceptions: Never make a U-turn in a business district, unless at an intersection or where a sign explicitly permits it.
